anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, the MIC26903YJL-TR (REG1) input-side pins are split across two nets: pins 13-16 (PVIN_1-4) are tied to the battery-input net VCC (which also feeds C1, C2 and R2), while pins 17-19 (PVIN_5-7), 27 (VIN), 28 (VDD) and 30 (PVIN_8) plus decoupling cap C4 are tied to a separate net labelled REG_VIN. No wire or global label joins REG_VIN to VCC anywhere on the root Power sheet (REG_VIN appears only on this sheet), so the controller's VIN/VDD and four of its eight PVIN pins are left floating.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the buck 'steps the battery input down to 5 V' from the XT60/VCC rail; all PVIN pins and the VIN pin of a synchronous buck must connect to the same battery input net (VCC) for the regulator to be powered and to start.

evidence.quote: Power sheet, REG1 MIC26903YJL-TR: '13 PVIN_1, 14 PVIN_2, 15 PVIN_3, 16 PVIN_4' wired to the VCC arrow (with C1/C2/R2); '17 PVIN_5, 18 PVIN_6, 19 PVIN_7, 27 VIN, 28 VDD, 30 PVIN_8' wired to the box net REG_VIN (with C4). No REG_VIN-to-VCC connection is drawn.
A MIC26903YJJ-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V.

anomalies.impact: The buck controller's supply/sense pins (VIN, VDD, PVIN_5-8) receive no input power, so the regulator cannot start. The 5 V rail (and therefore the 3.3 V LDO and the entire board) would be dead, or the part could be latched up / behave unpredictably.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the specification (R1=10 mΩ, L1=15 µH, R5/R6 giving ~5 V, correct I2C addresses, correct LDO/buck parts, the documented barometer pin-swap bug is not an anomaly), but the MIC26903 buck's VIN/VDD/PVIN_5-8 pins sit on a REG_VIN net that is never connected to the battery input VCC, leaving the regulator's power input floating - a deviation from the intended power stage.
